items.title: Admissible runs
items.note: admissible_iff: data x H g α c₁ c₂ are the data of some R : AdmissibleBFGSRun n F iff F is convex (ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ F; finite = real-valued) and n ≥ 1; every x_k is a differentiable point with g_k ≠ 0 and fderiv ℝ F (x k) v = dot (g k) v for all v (g_k = ∇F(x_k)); x_{k+1} = x_k + s_k and H_{k+1} = (I - s_ky_kᵀ/t_k)H_k(I - y_ks_kᵀ/t_k) + s_ks_kᵀ/t_k with s_k = -α_kH_kg_k, y_k = g_{k+1} - g_k, t_k = y_kᵀs_k (variables with defining equations); H_0 ≻ 0 (PosDef, symmetric); α_k > 0; 0 < c₁ < c₂ < 1; and the two non-strict inequalities of (art:aw). The structure omits n ≥ 1 (derived: dimension_pos) and stores the gradient as HasFDerivAt F (gradientFunctional (g k)) (x k). Lean's inverse is total, but t_k > 0 along every run (run_invariants), so (t k)⁻¹ = 1/t_k. Shared form for all modules: R : AdmissibleBFGSRun n F with s_k = R.displacement k, y_k = R.gradientChange k, t_k = R.curvature k, B_k = R.hessian k, q_k = R.q k, d_k = R.d k, β_k = R.beta k (run_notation).

inverseBFGS H s y is literally (1 - t⁻¹ • outer s y) * H * (1 - t⁻¹ • outer y s) + t⁻¹ • outer s s with t = dot y s, and bfgsStep H g α = -α • (H *ᵥ g) (library_formulas). update_formula states the display for every admissible run with s_k, y_k, t_k = R.displacement k, R.gradientChange k, R.curvature k.
The fields armijo and weak_wolfe of AdmissibleBFGSRun: F(x_{k+1}) ≤ F(x_k) + c₁g_kᵀs_k and g_{k+1}ᵀs_k ≥ c₂g_kᵀs_k (both non-strict), with 0 < c₁ < c₂ < 1 (fields c₁_pos, c₁_lt_c₂, c₂_lt_one).

The display defines B_k, q_k, d_k, Δ_k, ω and asserts -g_kᵀs_k = α_kq_k. notation_display states the assertion and that R.hessian k = (R.H k)⁻¹, R.q k = g_kᵀH_kg_k, R.d k = -g_kᵀs_k (R.d k is defined as α_k q_k). Δ_k and ω are written out as F (R.x k) - F (R.x (k + 1)) and 1 - R.c₂.

B̂_k is the variable Bhat with hBhat : ∀ k, Bhat k = R.hessian k - (R.q k)⁻¹ • outer (R.g k) (R.g k). "The objective values have a finite limit" is ∃ ℓ, Tendsto (fun k => F (R.x k)) atTop (𝓝 ℓ); ∑_k d_k < ∞ is Summable R.d (d_k > 0).

Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M39): end-of-proof mark. The library proves the lemma along this proof: fullBFGS_positive_invariants (induction on H_k ≻ 0 from the sum-of-squares form of the update and weak Wolfe), hessianUpdate (the Hessian identity), annihilatedMatrix_projection (B̂_k = PB_kPᵀ ⪰ 0, the metric Cauchy-Schwarz step) and annihilatedMatrix_mul_step (B̂_ks_k = 0).

items.title: Reference energy
items.note: r_k, E_k, a_k, R_k (Lean Rk, since R names the run) and F_* are variables with their defining equations; "x_* minimizes F" is ∀ z, F xstar ≤ F z.
E_k = r_kᵀB_kr_k, a_k = g_kᵀr_k and R_k = (y_kᵀr_{k+1})²/t_k with r_k = x_k - x_* are the library's referenceEnergy, referencePairing and referenceCorrection (reference_notation).

Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M39): end-of-proof mark. Undisplayed steps: a_k ≥ F(x_k) - F_* at a minimizer (gap_le_referencePairing), E_N ≥ 0 (referenceEnergy_nonneg), summation (gap_sq_mul_reciprocal_sum_le).
Stated with r_k = x_k - x_* and B̂_k (variable Bhat) of Lemma art:run-invariants.

Hypotheses as in the text: x_* minimizer, F_* = F(x_*), F(x_k) - F_* ≥ η > 0 for all k, R_k ≤ C for all k; conclusion for every N. These are the hypotheses of the reductio of lines 102-110: together with bounded gradients they cannot all hold (persistent_gap_contradiction; d_k → 0 follows from the minimizer by Armijo); without bounded gradients their satisfiability is not settled here. The proof is the finite-horizon form persistent_gap_budget_general, which assumes the gap only at N and R_k ≤ C only for k < N (exactly what the display's argument uses); its assumptions are satisfiable (example in the module: the quadratic run x_k = 2^{-k}, x_* = 0, N = 1, η = 1/8, C = 1).

principalSum H j is literally the sum of det H_{I,I} over the j-subsets I of Fin n (principalSum_def); e_{n+1}(H) = 0 is then a consequence (no (n+1)-subsets). The Lean definition is for every real matrix; the text restricts to symmetric H.

items.title: Principal-minor hierarchy
items.note: Standing assumptions written out with the shared forms of MatrixAlgebra.lean (hH, hs, hα, hq_def, hq, hβ_def, hβ, hHplus : Hplus = inverseBFGS H s y); ‖y‖² is sqNorm y; e_j is principalSum. Conclusion: the inequality for every 1 ≤ j ≤ n, and det H₊ = (α/β) det H. The j = n identity along runs is part of hessianInvariants.

Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M35, M39): Lemma art:gram-compression is cited with its appendix; end-of-proof mark. The library's principalMinorHierarchy follows this proof: an orthogonal eigenbasis (posDef_orthogonal_diagonalization), the compression bound for each selection Z_I (compressed_inverseBFGS_bound_generic, i.e. Lemma art:gram-compression), the eigenbasis sum (display 015) and orthogonal invariance (sum_transformed_coordinate_grams, principalSum_conjugate). The last assertion is the full-size case of Lemma art:gram-compression (MatrixAlgebra.full_dimension_case).

Under the assumptions of the theorem, for 1 ≤ j ≤ n and Z : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin j) ℝ with Zᵀ * Z = 1. Gram_H(y,Z) = [y Z]ᵀH[y Z] is metricGram H (fromCols (replicateCol Unit y) Z), as in MatrixAlgebra.lean, whose gram_compression states Lemma art:gram-compression in the same form.

The orthonormal eigenbasis is U with Uᵀ * U = 1 and H * U = U * diagonal lam (λ_i > 0); y_i are the coordinates yc = Uᵀ *ᵥ y; the j-column selection Z_I is U.submatrix id (fun i : I => i). All three relations (two equalities and the final inequality, with ‖y‖² = sqNorm y) are stated.

items.title: Reciprocal growth
items.note: "Bounded gradients" is ∃ Λ, ∀ k, ‖euclideanVector (R.g k)‖ ≤ Λ (the notion does not depend on the norm); d_k → 0 is Tendsto R.d atTop (𝓝 0). The limits are stated as written: (∏_{k<N} q_k⁻¹)^(1/N) (real power) and (1/N)∑_{k<N} q_k⁻¹ tend to +∞ (Tendsto ... atTop atTop). The library's reciprocalGrowth is for FullBFGSRun with a lower bound c ≤ β_k; the bridge is toFullBFGSRun with c = ω (beta_lower_bound).

Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M34, M39): display 017 defines β_k = −y_kᵀH_kg_k/q_k, the β of Theorem art:minor-hierarchy for the k-th update (R.beta k), so that β_k = t_k/d_k is an identity; the weighted sum is restricted to k ≥ J ("For k ≥ J, multiply ..."), where the remaining terms need d_k/ω ≤ η; end-of-proof mark. The library proves the theorem by the logarithmic form of this argument: one weighted potential V_η and tail per η (hierarchy_tail_potentials), the product bound of display 020 in log form (tail_log_product_upper), the fixed prefix (global_log_product_upper), and log u ≤ u - 1 in place of AM-GM (logMean_le_arithmeticMean). q_le_potential states the undisplayed q_k ≤ Λ² tr H_k ≤ Λ² V_η(H_k) (line 197).

Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M34): the display defines β_k = −y_kᵀH_kg_k/q_k (before, β_k was used without definition). Standing assumptions: those of the theorem, Λ > 0 with ‖g_k‖ ≤ Λ for all k, and K0 = 4Λ²/ω². β_k is R.beta k = -y_kᵀH_kg_k/q_k, as the display defines it; the conclusion is β_k = t_k/d_k, t_k/d_k ≥ ω, ‖y_k‖ ≤ 2Λ, α_k = d_k/q_k for every k.
For every k and 1 ≤ j ≤ n (the range of (art:hierarchy)), with K0 = 4Λ²/ω² and ω = 1 - R.c₂.
Adds η > 0 and J with d_k/ω ≤ η for k ≥ J. V_η is the variable V with V H = ∑_{j=1}^n (K0/η)^{j-1} e_j(H) for H ≻ 0 (Finset.Icc 1 n). The claim is V_η(H) > 0 for every H ≻ 0.
V_η(H_{k+1}) ≤ (2η/q_k)V_η(H_k) for k ≥ J, and ∏_{k=J}^{J+m-1} q_k⁻¹ ≥ 1/(Λ²V_η(H_J)(2η)^{m-1}) for every m ≥ 1 (the text leaves m ≥ 1 implicit; the product is over Finset.Ico J (J + m)).

eligiblePair_iff unfolds EligiblePair F c₁ c₂ x z g h to the display with the notation of lines 239-241 (g, h the gradients at the differentiable points x, z; s, y, d, Δ, t as variables with their defining equations) and ω = 1 - c₂: d > 0, c₁d ≤ Δ ≤ d, t ≥ ωd.

items.title: Band certificate
items.note: bandCertificate_iff (under the definition's standing assumptions K = {F ≤ b} compact, b > F_* = min F, 0 < c₁ < c₂ < 1, η > 0): a library BandCertificate on K_η with 0 ≤ C is exactly a field W : Vec n → Mat n and constants m > 0, C ≥ 0, L ≥ 0, δ > 0 with W(x) PSD (symmetric) at differentiable points of K_η, (art:visibility) at every differentiable point of K_η, and (art:secant-control), (art:transport) for all eligible pairs in K_η with d ≤ δ (A ⪯ B is (B - A).PosSemidef). The library's BandCertificate does not require C ≥ 0; hasBandCertificates_iff shows that "K admits the band certificates" (with C ≥ 0) is equivalent to the library's HasBandCertificates (any C), by replacing C with max{C,0} (t ≥ ωd > 0). The field is total but constrained only at differentiable band points, which is the text's field "on its differentiable points".

items.title: Transported comparison certificate
items.note: Hypotheses as in the text: K = {F ≤ b} compact, F_* = min F (IsLeast (Set.range F) Fstar), b > F_* (unused by the proof), K admits the band certificates of Definition art:band-certificate with C ≥ 0 (for the run's constants c₁, c₂, on which eligibility depends), x_0 ∈ K. Conclusions: F(x_k) → F_*, Euclidean dist(x_k, argmin F) → 0 (euclideanSolutionDistance), and x_k → x_* whenever x_* is the unique minimizer. The library's transportedCertificateConvergence needs neither C ≥ 0 nor b > F_*.

Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M35, M38, M39): the chain of the proof cites (art:visibility)–(art:transport) (before (art:secant-control)–(art:transport), leaving out the visibility bound it uses); display 025 is written m P̄⁻¹∑…; end-of-proof mark. Undisplayed steps stated in this module: iterates_in_band (Armijo keeps the run in K; with limiting gap ℓ > 0 every iterate is in K_{ℓ/2}), certificate_energy_nonneg (E_k ≥ 0), normalization_bounds (1 ≤ P_k ≤ P̄), finite_reciprocal_sum_le (dividing by P_{k+1} and summing). The library proves the theorem (transported_certificate_values) with the same trace step but the bound C(k+1) and its superquadratic theorem; the article's linear budget is ScalarTransport.reciprocal_sum_le, and certificate_budget_general here. Gradient bounds: bounded_gradients_of_compact_set; distance: euclidean_distance_to_argmin_of_values.

Standing assumptions: the theorem's hypotheses, limiting gap lim(F(x_k) - F_*) = ℓ > 0, the certificate Cert of K_{ℓ/2} with C ≥ 0 (W, m, C, L, δ = Cert.W, ...), J with d_k ≤ δ for k ≥ J, E_k = tr(B_kW(x_k)), and B̂_k. The chain (equality, two inequalities) is stated for every k ≥ J. These assumptions are those of a proof by contradiction and cannot all hold; the proof uses only certificate_step_general (one k, any band, x_k, x_{k+1} ∈ K_η, d_k ≤ δ), whose assumptions are satisfiable (example at the end of the module).

Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M38): m P̄⁻¹ in place of the fraction m/P̄. Standing assumptions of display 024 and P̄ = exp(L∑_{j≥J} d_j) (Pbar with its defining equation); the bound holds for every N ≥ J, with ∑_{k=J}^{N-1} over Finset.Ico J N. As for display 024 the assumptions cannot all hold; the proof uses certificate_budget_general (a finite window J ≤ k ≤ N in one band, ∑d_k < ∞), whose assumptions are satisfiable.

items.reason: Plan of the section (what the comparison energy is designed to measure); the precise statements are Lemma art:reference-energy and Definition art:band-certificate.

items.note: Informal reading of the energy identity E_{k+1}=E_k-a_k²/q_k+R_k: R_k is the secant cost, -a_k²/q_k the negative term measuring missed progress.

items.anchor: The matrix hierarchy then shows that, when the gradients are bounded, persistent
items.note: Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M32): the hypothesis "when the gradients are bounded" is stated. Summary of the contradiction of lines 102-110: with bounded gradients and d_k→0, a persistent gap and bounded secant corrections R_k≤C are incompatible (persistent_gap_contradiction).

items.anchor: The argument uses the matrices actually generated by BFGS throughout.
items.reason: Methodological remark: every Lean statement of this module about runs concerns the run's own matrices R.H k (no surrogate or limit matrices are assumed); no separate claim.

items.anchor: These are the usual actual-gradient, full-BFGS conventions
items.reason: Attribution of the conventions of Definition art:admissible to the literature (LO, XW).

items.anchor: A zero gradient is successful termination.
items.note: The mathematical content of calling a zero gradient a successful termination: at a differentiable point of a finite convex F with ∇F(x)=0, x is a global minimizer. The termination convention itself is part of the definition (admissible runs have nonzero gradients).

items.anchor: admissible runs do not assert that a differentiable acceptable point exists on
items.reason: Scope disclaimer: Definition art:admissible (AdmissibleBFGSRun) assumes a run and asserts nothing about the existence of acceptable points or about implementations.

items.anchor: The identity makes the intended contradiction visible.
items.note: The contradiction of the paragraph (lines 102-110), made precise: for an admissible run with bounded gradients and d_k→0, a minimizer x_*, and R_k≤C for all k, the gap F(x_k)-F_* cannot stay ≥η>0 for all k (display 010 against Theorem art:reciprocal-growth). The Lean statement includes the hypotheses of Theorem art:reciprocal-growth (bounded gradients, d_k→0). Since the correction M10 the paragraph names the bounded gradients (A/energy/prose/012); d_k→0 follows from Armijo, as x_* minimizes F.

items.anchor: Thus an objective-level bound on one component of a gradient jump would
items.note: Under the hypotheses of display 010 (minimizer x_*, gap ≥ η > 0 for all k, R_k ≤ C for all k): ∑_{k<N} q_k⁻¹ ≤ E_0/η² + (C/η²)N for every N. As for display 010, these hypotheses cannot all hold together with bounded gradients, and without bounded gradients their satisfiability is not settled here; the proof is the finite-horizon form reciprocal_sum_linear_general (gap at N, R_k ≤ C for k < N), whose assumptions are satisfiable (example in the module, N = 1).

items.anchor: proves that, along runs with bounded gradients, the full update requires
items.note: Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M10): the sentence names Theorem art:reciprocal-growth and its bounded gradients. reciprocal_sum_superlinear: bounded gradients and d_k → 0 exclude ∑_{k<N} q_k⁻¹ ≤ A + BN for all N; in the paragraph's setting, where x_* minimizes F and so d_k → 0 by Armijo, bounded gradients suffice (reciprocal_sum_superlinear_of_minimizer).

items.anchor: the initial energy is finite, and the
items.note: The asserted facts: E_k=r_k^TB_kr_k ≥ 0 for every k (and E_0 is a real number). "Neither step requires a bound on ‖B_k‖ or a limit for H_k" is visible in the statements: persistent_gap_budget and reciprocal_growth have no such hypothesis.

items.anchor: Multilinearity of the determinant identifies these sums with the coefficients of $\det(I+zH)$
items.note: For symmetric H (H.IsHermitian, i.e. Hᵀ=H for a real matrix): the z^j coefficient of the polynomial det(I+zH) is e_j(H) (proved by multilinearity of the determinant, det_one_add_smul_eq_sum_principal), so det(I+zH)=∑_{j=0}^n e_j(H)z^j for real z; e_j(QᵀHQ)=e_j(H) for orthogonal Q; e_j(H) = esymm_j of the eigenvalues (Multiset.esymm of hH.eigenvalues).

items.anchor: In particular $e_1=\tr$ and $e_n=\det$.
Trace and determinant potentials are central to classical BFGS analysis
items.reason: Literature context (FND_N92, FND_BN89); no claim is used.

items.anchor: The determinant records volume, while the intermediate
items.note: Made precise as: x↦Hx multiplies Lebesgue measure by |det H|; and for every orthonormal basis U and every j, e_j(H) is the sum of det(Z_IᵀHZ_I) over the j-column selections Z_I of U, i.e. of the determinants of the j-dimensional compressions of H.

items.note: Describes (art:hierarchy): e_j(H_+) is bounded by e_{j+1}(H) and e_j(H).

items.note: The positive weighted potential is V_η of the proof of Theorem art:reciprocal-growth (potential_pos, potential_contraction); no conditioning bound is assumed there.

items.anchor: Finite-horizon bounds
items.note: Both consequences of the companion's Theorem M:superquadratic (C/02_M/theorem/M:superquadratic), for admissible runs with bounded gradients ‖g_k‖ ≤ G (G > 0) and ∑_k d_k < ∞, ω = 1 - c₂. finite_horizon_bound is (M:finitehorizon): for every tail J, η > 0 and m ≥ 2, ∑_{k=J}^{J+m-1} q_k⁻¹ ≥ m [G² V_η(H_J)]^{-1/m} (η + D_J/(ω(m-1)))^{-(m-1)/m} with D_J = ∑_{k≥J} d_k, K_0 = 4G²/ω² and V_η(H) = ∑_{j=1}^n (K_0/η)^{j-1} e_j(H) (from the library's finiteHorizon, whose block length is m + 1). superquadratic_growth is (M:superquad): (∑_{k<N} q_k⁻¹)/N² → +∞.

resolved_discrepancies.description: The sentence "The next theorem proves that the full update requires faster growth" (energy.tex:108-110) means growth of ∑_{k<N} q_k⁻¹ faster than the linear bound of display A/energy/disp/010 (energy.tex:104-106). In text order the next theorem is Theorem art:minor-hierarchy (energy.tex:131-142), a one-step inequality for a single update that says nothing about the growth of ∑_{k<N} q_k⁻¹. The faster growth is Theorem art:reciprocal-growth, which assumes bounded gradients and d_k → 0; the paragraph (energy.tex:101-112) states neither. In its setting x_* minimizes F, so the values are bounded below and Armijo gives d_k → 0, but bounded gradients remain an extra hypothesis. With it the corrected claim holds: the reciprocal sum is not O(N) (Lean). The paragraph's contradiction (A/energy/prose/010) relies on the same hypothesis.
resolved_discrepancies.proposed: Theorem~\ref{art:reciprocal-growth} proves that, along runs with bounded gradients, the full update requires faster growth.
resolved_discrepancies.resolved: Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M10 in TODO_MANUSCRIPT_REVIEW.md); the description quotes the text before the correction, its line numbers are those after it.
